## Coverage and sources

The harvest contains 62 source headings:

- 30 included
- 16 inline
- 7 already published
- 1 deferred
- 8 out of scope

Likely challenges are Axler 9.40’s exterior-algebra machinery, Axler 9.51’s characteristic-polynomial criterion, OpenStax’s routine differentiation/integration drills, and Ricardo’s historical section. Result-specific reasons are recorded in the coverage file.

Primary treatments were [Axler](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf), [Interactive Linear Algebra](https://textbooks.math.gatech.edu/ila/ila.pdf), [OpenStax §6.7](https://openstax.org/books/calculus-volume-1/pages/6-7-integrals-exponential-functions-and-logarithms), [Ricardo](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359264337_The_Equivalence_of_Definitions_of_the_Natural_Logarithm_Function), and [Lee’s notes](https://math.hawaii.edu/~lee/calculus/Logarithm.pdf). [Vrabel’s matrix-determinant-lemma paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1608.03207) backs the rank-one formula; the scaffold independently widens it to commutative rings.

All 67 formal published dependencies were opened, confirmed published, and read at their actual Definition/Statement/Example. Their individual `component-lit`, `component-adapted/source`, or `component-adapted/knowledge` routes are enumerated in the notes. Two related B-page items were also opened but deliberately excluded from the dependency graph.

## Findings

- The published determinant page does not contain cofactors, Laplace expansion, the adjugate, or Cramer’s rule despite the dispatch’s description. The scaffold therefore builds them locally.
- The initial rational-function-field route for singular adjugates was removed. Rank-one determinant updates now prove similarity equivariance without undeveloped machinery.
- Ring statements use “determinant is a unit”; “nonzero” is reserved for fields.
- Positive-size cofactor results explicitly need the empty-minor convention, while operator determinant separately covers dimension zero.
- Literature’s one-based indices are converted to the library’s zero-based convention.
- OpenStax’s substitution proof is not used; the product law follows by differentiating \(L(xy)-L(x)\).
- Before identification, no proof uses `exp` or `log`. Functional-equation arguments transport through \(E\); the only construction bridge is exponential IVP uniqueness.
- Existing B-page examples are not formal dependencies.

No split is proposed: the A pages contain 18 and 19 items. There are no forward references, cross-batch dependencies, unresolved dependencies, B-page dependencies, or blockers.
